title: Drive unit internal fault
shortDescription: Generic internal fault in the Brose drive unit.
fullDescription:
F01 is a generic internal error on the Brose Drive S / S Mag motor. Often caused by a transient electrical fault or firmware glitch.

Power cycle first. If the error persists, take the bike to a certified dealer for firmware flashing.

fixSteps.title: Dealer firmware update
fixSteps.instruction: Have dealer connect Brose Service Tool.

whenToCallPro: If power cycle does not clear the fault.

faq.a: Not always; often a reset clears it.

title: Motor temperature error
fullDescription:
F02 is displayed when the Brose motor hits its thermal cutoff. Assist is disabled to protect the windings.

Let the motor cool for 10-20 minutes before resuming.

fixSteps.title: Rest motor
fixSteps.instruction: Stop and let the motor cool for 15 minutes.

whenToCallPro: If fault returns at low loads.

faq.a: Not if you let it cool and avoid repeated trips.

title: Torque sensor error
fullDescription:
F03 typically results from a pedal being loaded during power-on, causing a bad torque-sensor zero. Restart with no load on the pedals.

If it returns, a dealer recalibration is needed.

fixSteps.title: Restart unloaded
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, remove feet from pedals, power on.

faq.a: Very cold temperatures can temporarily shift the reading.

title: Speed sensor error
fullDescription:
F04 is the Brose speed-sensor fault. Check spoke magnet alignment and sensor integrity on the chainstay.

Common after wheel or tire service where the magnet was knocked off.

fixSteps.title: Align magnet
fixSteps.instruction: Position magnet with 5-8 mm gap to sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If cracked, replace sensor with Brose or bike-brand OEM part.

whenToCallPro: If wiring routes inside the frame.

faq.q: Can a strong magnet boost signal?
faq.a: Use only approved magnets for accuracy.

title: Battery communication error
shortDescription: Battery not detected or not responding.
fullDescription:
F05 appears when the drive unit cannot read data from the battery. Dirty contacts or a loose cable are typical culprits.

Remove and clean battery contacts, check that the battery seats fully.

fixSteps.title: Clean contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Use contact cleaner on battery and frame contacts.

fixSteps.title: Reseat battery
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure battery locks fully into place.

faq.a: Possibly; test with a known-good battery if you have access.

title: Display communication error
shortDescription: Display and drive unit are not communicating.
fullDescription:
F06 indicates a lost connection between the display and the motor. Usually a loose cable at the handlebar or motor.

Reseat the display cable on both ends.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cables
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and replug the display cable.

faq.a: Usually not; it is typically a cable.

title: Hall sensor error
shortDescription: Motor Hall sensor fault inside the drive unit.
fullDescription:
F07 is a motor-internal fault. The Hall-effect sensors that detect motor rotor position are giving bad readings. This requires a dealer.

Do not attempt to open the sealed motor.

fixSteps.title: Dealer service
fixSteps.instruction: Take to authorized dealer for motor service or replacement.

faq.a: Usually not; the motor must be opened.

title: Overcurrent error
fullDescription:
F08 is triggered when the motor phase current exceeds a protection limit. Often happens during hard starts on a steep hill.

Restart the system; if persistent, have the motor tested.
whenToCallPro: If F08 returns under light load.

title: Voltage out of range
shortDescription: Supply voltage too high or too low.
fullDescription:
F09 indicates the motor is seeing a voltage outside its operating range. Can mean a weak battery, a bad charger, or a poor battery connection.

Fully charge the battery and check contacts.
whenToCallPro: If battery is suspect, have it tested.

title: Critical motor fault
fullDescription:
F10 is a severe fault requiring service. The motor refuses to operate until it has been inspected.

Do not ride under assist. Transport the bike to a dealer.

faq.a: Often yes if within warranty period.
